mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a supply shock, which disrupts production and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, boosting corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS increase and UNRATE decrease on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2%) signals a stable economic backdrop, which encourages risk-taking and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strong housing market, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following two consecutive months of HOUST increase, or the correlation between HOUST increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
